children: The Cross River State Government has unveiled plans to develop a livestock economy projected to be worth more than N100 billion under a proposed seven-year development roadmap for the sector.

The Special Adviser to Governor Bassey Otu on Livestock Development, Liyel Imoukhuede, disclosed this in Calabar while outlining the government’s plans to transform livestock production into a major source of employment, investment, food and income for residents.

Imoukhuede said the proposed roadmap would focus on increasing productivity, improving animal health, developing infrastructure, promoting value addition, attracting private investment, expanding market access and strengthening food security.

He explained that the plan was designed to move livestock production from largely subsistence activities to a structured and commercially driven industry covering cattle, dairy, poultry, pigs, sheep and goats, aquaculture, feed production, processing, cold-chain logistics and livestock markets.
According to him, the immediate phase of the programme would involve the enumeration of farmers, stakeholder engagement and an assessment of the state’s livestock resources.
He added that strengthening veterinary services, land and ranching planning, mobilising investment and completing the livestock development roadmap would also form part of the initial phase.
The Special Adviser said the medium-term phase would focus on expanding production, infrastructure, processing capacity, employment opportunities and access to markets.

He said the government was also assessing existing livestock assets and identifying investment opportunities in cattle, dairy, poultry, feed production, meat processing, cold-chain facilities, breeding and livestock markets.
Imoukhuede said Cross River’s agricultural land, strategic location, international border and existing agricultural assets could position the state as a major livestock production and export hub.

He further disclosed that the state was working with the Federal Government and development partners through initiatives including the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) to strengthen the sector.

According to him, the roadmap is expected to form part of the state government’s broader strategy to attract private capital into agriculture while creating economic opportunities for young people and women.

The proposed plan is also in line with the Federal Government’s livestock transformation agenda, which prioritises state-specific investment, private-sector participation, animal health, feed and water development, processing and stronger livestock value chains.

The government said the initiative, if implemented, would increase the contribution of livestock to the Cross River economy and strengthen the sector’s role alongside other key areas such as agriculture and tourism.
